question: 35-year-old woman on hormonal treatment for infertility. He went to the emergency department due to constitutional syndrome and paresthesias in the left side of the body. In blood tests, Hb 7.5 g / dL, reticulocytes 10% (0.52%), platelets 5,000 / uL, normal leukocytes, LDH 1,200 IU / L, direct negative Coombs test, undetectable haptoglobin are detected. Morphology of peripheral blood with abundant schistocytes. Normal coagulation tests. What is the diagnostic suspicion and the most appropriate treatment?

options.opb: Von Willebrand disease. Administration of desmopressin.
options.opc: Thrombocytopenic purpura. Start steroids and platelet transfusion.
options.ope: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura. Treatment with plasmapheresis.

analysis: The clinical presentation with constitutional symptoms, paresthesias, low Hb, high reticulocytes, low platelets, high LDH, schistocytes in peripheral blood, and undetectable haptoglobin points towards a diagnosis of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP). This is a medical emergency requiring immediate intervention.
